summary: An array stores a list of values in one variable. Bash has indexed arrays (numbered from 0) and associative arrays (looked up by a name).
notes: ${#songs[@]} is the number of items. ${songs[-1]} is the last item.
"${songs[@]}" with double quotes is the safe way to loop. It keeps "Blue in Green" together as one item.
Associative arrays need declare -A first. Without it, bash treats Maya as the number 0 and every name writes to the same slot.
pitfall: $songs without an index is only the first item, So What. Use "${songs[@]}" for all items and ${#songs[@]} for the count.
